`add_boundary` now tells your assistant the rules the AtlasFetch API actually enforces, so it builds valid shapes the first time.

## Changed

- **`add_boundary` description** covers what the tool does, that each call creates a new boundary, the prerequisites (the set must exist; making it queryable happens in the dashboard), and what happens at plan limits.
- **Polygon-only geometry is now enforced before any request.** The input schema is typed: `type` must be `"Polygon"`, and each ring needs at least 4 `[longitude, latitude]` positions. A MultiPolygon, a GeoJSON Feature or a short ring is refused immediately with a clear message instead of costing a round trip.
- **The demo key's limits are stated up front:** 5 positions per polygon, properties restricted to `category`, `color` and `priority`, and one set shared by every demo user that drops its oldest boundary when full. Don't upload anything private with the demo key.
- **`add_boundary` is now marked potentially destructive**, because adding to the full shared demo set deletes the oldest boundary.
- **`list_boundary_sets`** correctly describes granted keys as id and label.

`lookup_location` is unchanged.

## Install

**Claude Desktop** — download `atlasfetch-0.1.3.mcpb` below and open it. The API key field is optional.

**Claude Code**

```
claude mcp add atlasfetch -- npx -y atlasfetch-mcp
```

**Other clients** — `npx -y atlasfetch-mcp`, with `ATLASFETCH_API_KEY` in the server's env. See the [README](https://github.com/atlasfetch-dev/atlasfetch-mcp#install).

No signup needed to try it: without a key it uses a shared demo key capped at 1,000 lookups a month across everyone using it. Get your own limits with a free sign-up at [atlasfetch.xyz](https://atlasfetch.xyz/dashboard).
